walkthroughs.body_html: Paris Agreement (2015) signed by 196 parties. Each submits Nationally Determined Contributions. UNEP Gap Report (2023): current NDCs put world on 2.5-2.9 degrees C path; need 43 percent cut by 2030 vs 2019 levels for 1.5 degrees C. COP28 (Dubai 2023) agreed transition away from fossil fuels.

Boundary Dam (Canada 2014) captures 1 Mt CO2/yr from coal plant. Climeworks Orca (Iceland 2021) direct air capture 4000 t/yr. BECCS modelled as essential for 1.5 degrees C scenarios but unproven at scale. Solar PV cost fell 90 percent 2010-2020.

Reforestation can sequester ~10 Gt C globally if 350 Mha restored (Bonn Challenge). Mangrove and saltmarsh restoration stores blue carbon. UK peatland restoration target: 280000 ha by 2050. Co-benefits include biodiversity, flood risk reduction.

mcqs.q: How do humans affect the carbon cycle?
options: Humans only affect the carbon cycle by breathing out CO2.
It is the process of rain falling from clouds.
Humans affect the carbon cycle by eating plants.
By burning fossil fuels (releasing stored geological carbon to the atmosphere) and deforestation (reducing the biosphere store and releasing carbon).

mcqs.q: Why are tropical rainforest soils typically infertile?
options: Heavy rainfall leaches nutrients, and most nutrients are stored in living biomass and rapidly recycled — the soil itself holds very little.
Because so much vegetation grows there, the soil must be fertile.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.
Humans affect the carbon cycle by eating plants.
Humans affect the carbon cycle by eating plants.
It is only water evaporating from puddles and lakes.
The combined loss of water from a surface through evaporation (from soil and water bodies) and transpiration (from plant leaves).
It is the process of rain falling from clouds.
